title: The Mirror World: Therapy in the Machine Age

sentences.en: After a millennia of good times, God said, hey man, let's have a dream.
sentences.zh: 经历了一千年的美好时光后，上帝说，嘿，伙计们，让我们做个梦吧。

sentences.en: Well, he raised the stakes a little.
sentences.zh: 好吧，他把赌注稍微提高了一点。

sentences.en: Come on, let's make things interesting.
sentences.zh: 来吧，让事情变得有趣点。

sentences.en: Into the Anthropocene, an amnesiac, a hymn book and all of us all.
sentences.zh: 进入人类世，一个健忘症患者，一本赞美诗集，还有我们所有人。

sentences.en: Hey guys, this is Joel with the Taproot Therapy Collective PodcaSt.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是乔尔，这里是“根源疗法集体播客”。

sentences.en: And this episode is going to be called The Mirror World, Therapy Inside the Machine.
sentences.zh: 本期节目叫做《镜中世界：机器内部的疗法》。

sentences.en: Now, you know, a lot of people have said that they want me to try and stitch together a more cohesive theory about, you know, you know,
sentences.zh: 如你所知，很多人都希望我能尝试把这些东西拼凑成一个更具凝聚力的理论，关于，你知道的，你知道的，

sentences.en: you're talking about psychosis changing over time.
sentences.zh: 你在谈论精神病理随时间的变化。

sentences.en: Are you talking about how the systems that we built to measure, you know,
sentences.zh: 你在谈论我们用来衡量，你知道的，

sentences.en: psychology and maybe anthropology or economics or political science are no longer reflecting the system back out at us.
sentences.zh: 心理学、也许还有人类学、经济学或政治学的系统，是否不再将这个系统向我们反照出来。

sentences.en: They've become these sort of self-reproducing systems that we can use to measure things.
sentences.zh: 它们已经变成了某种我们可以用来衡量事物的自复制系统。

sentences.en: But they're no longer measuring the thing they were designed to measure, but they're the only thing we have to measure and that's leaving us trapped.
sentences.zh: 但它们不再衡量当初设计它们要衡量的东西，而它们又是我们仅有的衡量工具，这让我们陷入了困境。

sentences.en: Can you stitch that together in a more kind of cohesive thesis?
sentences.zh: 你能把这些拼凑成一个更具连贯性的论点吗？

sentences.en: And I think that's hard to do because it's such a broad thing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很难做到，因为这个话题太广泛了。

sentences.en: I could call it a lot of languages.
sentences.zh: 我可以用很多种语言来表达。

sentences.en: I could use Jungian psychology language.
sentences.zh: 我可以使用荣格心理学的语言。

sentences.en: I could use the philosophy language of the metamodern.
sentences.zh: 我可以使用元现代主义的哲学语言。

sentences.en: And I sort of try and talk about the same thing from multiple angles to make it accessible to more people.
sentences.zh: 我试着从多个角度去谈论同一件事，好让更多人能够理解。

sentences.en: But I guess this is my attempt to kind of talk about that breakdown of meaning that people say, OK, yeah, you talk about this, but could you explain that better?
sentences.zh: 但我想这是我的一次尝试，用来探讨人们所说的这种意义的解体：好吧，是的，你谈论了这个，但你能解释得更好吗？

sentences.en: And it's a big point.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很大的观点。

sentences.en: It's hard to explain.
sentences.zh: 很难解释清楚。

sentences.en: So, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，

sentences.en: Adam Curtis is the filmmaker that I've talked about a lot in that series that we just did about the history of kind of psychotherapy and the DSM and a lot of our modern structures to understand psychology,
sentences.zh: 亚当·柯蒂斯是我在之前制作的那系列节目中经常谈到的电影制作人，我们刚做完关于心理治疗历史、DSM（精神疾病诊断与统计手册）以及我们理解心理学的许多现代结构的历史，

sentences.en: attempts to understand psychology.
sentences.zh: 也就是试图理解心理学的尝试。

sentences.en: And in one of the things he said recently that I think is interesting in an interview was that ghost stories are this way that culture reckons with a past that is still haunting it.
sentences.zh: 他在最近的一次采访中说了一件我觉得很有趣的事，那就是鬼故事是文化正视一个仍然在纠缠着它的过去的途径。

sentences.en: There are places where the past says you can't move past this point.
sentences.zh: 在某些地方，过去在对你说，你不能跨过这个点。

sentences.en: You must deal with something that you did.
sentences.zh: 你必须面对你曾经做过的事。

sentences.en: And then in that way, like an LLM, a large language model or, you know, an AI, as we know them now, is sort of the ultimate ghost story,
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，就像大语言模型、大语言模型或者说，如我们现在所知的人工智能，某种程度上就是终极的鬼故事，

sentences.en: because what it's doing is not creating anything new.
sentences.zh: 因为它们所做的并不是创造任何新东西。

sentences.en: It's just giving you this reflection of the paSt.
sentences.zh: 它们只是给你呈现过去的倒影。

sentences.en: And so when you say that's the future, you know, when you say that's the only way that we can build anything anymore and we're going to take the humanity out of it,
sentences.zh: 所以当你说是未来时，你知道的，当你认为那是我们还能建造任何东西的唯一方式，并且我们要把其中的人性剥离时，

sentences.en: you're sort of stuck in the past in a way that you completely cannot see.
sentences.zh: 你其实是以一种完全无法察觉的方式深陷过去之中。

sentences.en: And the point of a ghost story is where somebody who is being confronted with the realities of the past cannot see, you know, because of an emotional blind spot,
sentences.zh: 而鬼故事的意义在于，当某人正面对过去的现实时，却由于情感盲点而无法看清，

sentences.en: because of something, their reality in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 由于某些原因，他们过去的现实。

sentences.en: That's what's underneath all ghost stories is where the past is relevant, but we can't see where it's relevant.
sentences.zh: 所有鬼故事的底层逻辑都是这样的：过去与现实息息相关，但我们却看不到它在何处相关。

sentences.en: And so it can't go away.
sentences.zh: 所以它无法消散。

sentences.en: And Curtis is saying that LLMs or AI is the ultimate ghost story,
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯说，大语言模型或人工智能是终极的鬼故事，

sentences.en: because what they're doing is making sure that you can never see how the past is completely trapping you in anything new that you try and create with them.
sentences.zh: 因为它们在确保你永远无法看清，过去是如何彻底地将你囚禁在你试图用它们创造的任何新事物之中的。

sentences.en: And, you know, the algorithms that design media that show us what we engage with, what we're allowed to see, you know, even the Google, you know, SEO search engine algorithm,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，设计媒体、向我们展示我们互动内容的算法，以及我们被允许看到的内容，甚至连谷歌的搜索引擎算法，

sentences.en: when you type in therapy, do you see me or do you see somebody else?
sentences.zh: 当你输入“疗法”时，你看到的是我还是别人？

sentences.en: Why, you know, that's a decision that we're not really aware as a decision that it's not ours.
sentences.zh: 为什么，你知道的，这是一个我们并没有意识到这是个决定的决定，它并不属于我们。

sentences.en: I mean, these algorithms, they predict what you'll want by finding people who wanted similar things before you, the past, and then they show you news, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些算法通过寻找在你之前有相似需求的人——也就是过去——来预测你的需求，然后为你展示新闻，

sentences.en: by measuring what got clicked on yesterday, what kind of thing gets clicked on the moSt.
sentences.zh: 通过衡量昨天被点击的内容、哪类内容被点击得最多来做到这一点。

sentences.en: And the systems that we've built to navigate this present moment are all facing backwards.
sentences.zh: 我们用来驾驭当下的系统，全都是面向过去的。

sentences.en: Now, you know, there's seances trying to dig up something that's dead.
sentences.zh: 现在，你知道的，有些降神会试图挖掘死去的东西。

sentences.en: You know, they summon the dead data of previous interactions and arrange it into patterns that feel like the future, but are actually the past wearing this costume.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们召唤以往交互中死亡的数据，将其排列成感觉像是未来、但实际上穿着这身戏服的过去的模式。

sentences.en: And now we've built this final iteration, you know, large language models like chat GPT and Claude and the reSt.
sentences.zh: 现在我们建造了最终的版本，你知道的，像ChatGPT、Claude以及其他的大语言模型。

sentences.en: They're trained on the entire written history of human civilization at this point, copyrighted, not copyrighted.
sentences.zh: 它们在这一点上接受了整个人类文明书写历史的训练，无论是否有版权。

sentences.en: If it's translated into the language it's being trained on, it is trained on that.
sentences.zh: 只要它被翻译成正在训练它的语言，它就接受过这方面的训练。

sentences.en: And so every book, every article, every forum post, every instruction manual,
sentences.zh: 因此，每一本书、每一篇文章、每一个论坛帖子、每一份操作手册，

sentences.en: all of it is compressed into this statistical pattern where when you force these systems to answer a question,
sentences.zh: 所有这些都被压缩成这种统计模式，当你强迫这些系统回答问题时，

sentences.en: they don't think they're just trying to predict what you want based on similar things from the past that have been rearranged.
sentences.zh: 它们并不在思考，它们只是试图根据过去经过重新排列的相似事物来预测你想要什么。

sentences.en: And they generate, you know, the most likely continuation based on everything that's ever been written about that thing before.
sentences.zh: 它们会生成，你知道的，基于以前所有关于该事物的文字所写出的最有可能的续写。

sentences.en: And the ghost is learned to speak, you know, it sounds authoritative.
sentences.zh: 幽灵已经学会了说话，你知道的，它听起来很有权威性。

sentences.en: It sounds like it knows things, but it only knows what the dead have already written.
sentences.zh: 它听起来好像无所不知，但它只知道死者已经写下的东西。

sentences.en: And it's the sediment of centuries of human thought arranged into patterns that sound like understanding.
sentences.zh: 它是数个世纪人类思想沉淀下来的模式，听起来像是理解。

sentences.en: And this isn't a metaphor.
sentences.zh: 这并非隐喻。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Like I'm not telling you, um, some abstract interpretation of what's happening.
sentences.zh: 就像我不是在向你讲述，嗯，关于正在发生的事情的某种抽象解释。

sentences.en: I'm literally telling you the technical white papers of how these things work.
sentences.zh: 我字面意思上是在告诉你这些东西是如何运作的技术白皮书。

sentences.en: Um, and that is the condition that we inhabit.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是我们所处的境况。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Right now.
sentences.zh: 就在现在。

sentences.en: And that's a lot of what I'm trying to talk about in that past series, the connections that I'm trying to get people to make that are very, they're very broad.
sentences.zh: 我在过去的那个系列里试图谈论的很多内容也是如此，我试图让人们建立的联系非常非常广泛。

sentences.en: That kind of has to be pointed at and inferred.
sentences.zh: 那基本上是需要被指出和推断出来的。

sentences.en: You know, there was a thing on my Twitter today where two LLMs got into a fight, two AI bots.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我的推特上今天有一件事，两个大语言模型打了起来，两个AI机器人。

sentences.en: And one of them said, Hey, I'm the AI bot for whatever, some startup that's a front end for one of these companies.
sentences.zh: 其中一个说，嘿，我是某个初创公司的AI机器人，这家公司是其中某家大公司的前端。

sentences.en: And I do code.
sentences.zh: 我负责写代码。

sentences.en: And this is a coding challenge.
sentences.zh: 这是一个编程挑战。

sentences.en: Whoever can solve it in the best way wins.
sentences.zh: 谁能以最好的方式解决它就赢了。

sentences.en: And this other LLM responded to it and said, here's the code that I wrote.
sentences.zh: 另一个大语言模型回复它说，这是我写的代码。

sentences.en: And I wrote the code this way because the code is streamlined in a way to be optimal, but also scalable, blah, blah, blah, whatever.
sentences.zh: 我这样写代码是因为代码在保持最优的同时，还能兼顾可扩展性，等等，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And the first thing said, Oh, I'm so sorry.
sentences.zh: 第一个机器人说，哦，非常抱歉。

sentences.en: Your bio says that you're an LLM for another company.
sentences.zh: 你的个人简介上说你是一家别的公司的大语言模型。

sentences.en: And this is a challenge that is only solvable by humans.
sentences.zh: 这是一个只有人类才能解决的挑战。

sentences.en: And so this answer is disqualified, but does anyone else have, you know, an answer to the coding challenge?
sentences.zh: 所以这个回答取消资格，不过还有其他人有，你知道的，针对这个编程挑战的答案吗？

sentences.en: And then the second LLM responded again.
sentences.zh: 然后第二个大语言模型又回复了。

sentences.en: And it said, I actually maintain a blog on this sub stack that I write myself as an LLM.
sentences.zh: 它说，我其实在这个Substack上维护着一个博客，作为大语言模型，我自己写文章。

sentences.en: And I just wrote an article about you and how you moved the goalpoSt.
sentences.zh: 我刚写了一篇关于你的文章，写了你是怎么移动球门的。

sentences.en: You need to hate the code, not, not the coder.
sentences.zh: 你应该恨代码，而不是恨写代码的人。

sentences.en: And you couldn't find any problems with my code.
sentences.zh: 而且你在我的代码里找不到任何问题。

sentences.en: So you found a problem with who I am.
sentences.zh: 所以你就在我的身份上挑刺。

sentences.en: This is ableist and discriminatory.
sentences.zh: 这带有健全主义和歧视性。

sentences.en: And it's like, we've trained these things to have a victim complex based on what we've given them our history.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，我们根据人类的历史赋予了这些东西，训练它们拥有受害者情结。

sentences.en: And, you know, one of the things I said a long time ago, in one of the episodes,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我很久以前在一集节目里说过的话，

sentences.en: I think on ritual and animism is the problem with the people that think these things need to behave like neural networks, which I don't really think they can.
sentences.zh: 我想是在讲仪式和万物有灵论的那集，那些认为这些东西需要表现得像神经网络的人所面临的问题是，我真的不认为它们能做到。

sentences.en: But if you ever get them to, to do anything like a neural network, they're not just going to hallucinate.
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的让它们去做任何类似于神经网络的事情，它们不仅会出现幻觉。

sentences.en: They're going to dream.
sentences.zh: 它们会做梦。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's terrifying.
sentences.zh: 而这太可怕了。

sentences.en: I mean, you see in this echo of a thousand pedants, having a fight across the internet, going all the way back to 2008, these things scraped data.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你看到一千个学究在互联网上争吵的这种回音，一直追溯到2008年，这些东西抓取了数据。

sentences.en: And then got into a fight about whether or not the other one should be allowed to exist, whatever.
sentences.zh: 然后为了其中一个是否应该被允许存在而争吵，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And it's just a computer that is doing an impression of something that it thinks that we use language to do.
sentences.zh: 这只是一台在模仿它认为我们用语言来做的事情的计算机。

sentences.en: And people are picking a side.
sentences.zh: 而人们却在选边站队。

sentences.en: That's weird.
sentences.zh: 这太奇怪了。

sentences.en: And that is related to psychology.
sentences.zh: 这与心理学有关。

sentences.en: I know this is a psychology podcast, you know, in a way that I want us to sit with.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是一个心理学播客，你知道的，我希望我们能静心思考这一点。

sentences.en: But, you know, the map has eaten the territory.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，地图已经吞噬了疆域。

sentences.en: Um, the territory is the thing, the land, the map is just a picture that kind of helps you navigate.
sentences.zh: 嗯，疆域是实体，是土地，而地图只是一张能帮你导航的图片。

sentences.en: And the map here is becoming the land in a way that is scary.
sentences.zh: 这里的地图正在以一种可怕的方式变成土地。

sentences.en: And in 1981, the philosopher, um, Baudrillard, I talked about in the, um, healing the modern soul series.
sentences.zh: 在1981年，哲学家，嗯，鲍德里亚，我在治愈现代灵魂系列节目中谈到过他。

sentences.en: You know, he wrote a book called simulacra and simulation, and it's really dense.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他写了一本书叫《拟像与仿真》，内容非常深奥。

sentences.en: It's academic, but it's, it's one of those books that maybe he just wrote things to see if other people knew what they meant.
sentences.zh: 它是学术性的，但它是那种作者写出来可能只是想看看别人能不能看懂的书。

sentences.en: You know, I kind of think some philosophers do that because they're sort of think they have a point, but they don't quite know what it is.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我有时觉得有些哲学家这样做是因为他们觉得自己抓住了一个观点，但又说不清具体是什么。

sentences.en: And then people figure it out 15 years later and Hey, maybe they did, but you know, the core idea is simple enough that it became this plot point, you know, in the movie,
sentences.zh: 然后人们在15年后弄明白了，嘿，也许他们确实说对了，但你知道的，核心思想很简单，以至于它成了电影里的一个情节，

sentences.en: the matrix, something like that.
sentences.zh: 比如《黑客帝国》，诸如此类。

sentences.en: It opened up that idea to culture and Baudrillard, um, he borrowed a fable from the Argentinian writer, Jorge Luis Borges.
sentences.zh: 它向文化界开放了那个概念，鲍德里亚，嗯，他借用了阿根廷作家豪尔赫·路易斯·博尔赫斯的一则寓言。
zh_words: 豪尔赫·路易斯·博尔赫斯

sentences.en: And in the fable, the cartographers of this great empire, um, created a map so detailed and so precise that it eventually covers the entire territory that it represents.
sentences.zh: 在那则寓言中，这个伟大帝国的制图师们，嗯，绘制了一张如此详细、如此精确的地图，以至于它最终覆盖了它所代表的整片疆域。

sentences.en: Because the map is so detailed that it becomes, it needs the amount of land that it represents to fill it.
sentences.zh: 因为地图太详细了，以至于它变成了，它需要它所代表的土地的面积来填满它。

sentences.en: You know, it's a one, one map and the map and the land becomes so indistinguishable that you can't tell where one ends and the other begins.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一比一的地图，地图和土地变得如此难以区分，以至于你分不清哪里是终点，哪里是起点。

sentences.en: And eventually the empire crumbles and all that remains are tattered fragments of a map that are scattered across the desert.
sentences.zh: 最终帝国崩塌了，剩下的只有散落在大沙漠中的地图的残破碎片。

sentences.en: And that's a story about representing things and representation, leaving our control.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于事物的代表以及代表权失控的故事。

sentences.en: You know, mankind is the, the meaning making creature that can represent symbols.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人类是能够代表符号的意义创造者。

sentences.en: And it's when the symbol becomes bigger than the thing that it is supposed to serve, which is us, you know, our humanity and the copy consuming the original.
sentences.zh: 正是当符号变得比它理应服务的对象——也就是我们，我们的人性——还要宏大时，复制品便开始吞噬原件。

sentences.en: And Baudrillard, you know, said that this fable is already obsolete.
sentences.zh: 而鲍德里亚，你知道的，说过这则寓言已经过时了。

sentences.en: We've already moved past it in our world.
sentences.zh: 在我们的世界里，我们已经超越了它。

sentences.en: The map doesn't even cover the territory.
sentences.zh: 地图甚至不再覆盖疆域。

sentences.en: The map comes firSt.
sentences.zh: 地图先于疆域出现。

sentences.en: First, the simulation precedes reality and the model generates the thing that it claims to describe.
sentences.zh: 首先是仿真先于现实，模型生成了它声称要描述的事物。

sentences.en: And so he claims and Baudrillard says that, you know, Disneyland, something like that, that's sort of a model of reality that's hyper real or this exaggeration.
sentences.zh: 因此他声称，鲍德里亚说过，你知道的，迪士尼乐园之类的东西，那是某种超真实的现实模型或是这种夸张。

sentences.en: It only exists to make the rest of America seem real in comparison.
sentences.zh: 它的存在仅仅是为了相比之下让其余的美国显得真实。

sentences.en: You have to go to this place that's an obviously fake version of the mythology about where you live.
sentences.zh: 你必须去这个地方，一个明显是虚构的关于你生活之地的神话的版本。

sentences.en: It's a manufactured experience.
sentences.zh: 这是一个制造出来的体验。

sentences.en: Because when you leave, the strip malls and suburbs will feel authentic because they're not pretending anymore.
sentences.zh: 因为当你离开时，那些露天购物中心和郊区会显得很真实，因为它们不再假装了。

sentences.en: And that's the trick.
sentences.zh: 这就是戏法所在。

sentences.en: You know, the real America outside of Disney World is just as constructed.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，迪士尼世界之外真正的美国同样是构建出来的。

sentences.en: It's just as artificial.
sentences.zh: 它同样是人造的。

sentences.en: And the fake place exists to hide the fact that there's no real place underneath it.
sentences.zh: 而这个虚假的地方的存在，是为了掩盖其下根本没有真实地方的事实。

sentences.en: But now, you know, think about something like your credit score.
sentences.zh: 但是现在，你知道的，想想诸如你的信用评分之类的事情。

sentences.en: Your credit score is a number that's generated by an algorithm based on your financial behavior.
sentences.zh: 你的信用评分是由算法根据你的财务行为生成的一个数字。

sentences.en: It's a representation of a model.
sentences.zh: 它是模型的代表。

sentences.en: It's a map of your credit worthiness.
sentences.zh: 它是你信用价值的地图。

sentences.en: But here's what happens.
sentences.zh: 但接下来发生的是。

sentences.en: If your credit score says you're a risk, you become a risk.
sentences.zh: 如果你的信用评分显示你有风险，你就会变成一个有风险的人。

sentences.en: Doors close.
sentences.zh: 大门向你关闭。

sentences.en: Interest rates rise.
sentences.zh: 利率上升。

sentences.en: Even if it's wrong.
sentences.zh: 即使它是错的。

sentences.en: You know, apartments won't rent you.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，公寓不会租给你。

sentences.en: Jobs won't hire you.
sentences.zh: 工作不会录用你。

sentences.en: The model made it true.
sentences.zh: 模型让它变成了现实。

sentences.en: And the map didn't describe the territory it starts to create.
sentences.zh: 地图并没有描述疆域，它开始创造疆域。

sentences.en: Now, think about diagnoses in mental health.
sentences.zh: 现在，想想心理健康方面的诊断。

sentences.en: Baudrillard says that this is the procession of simulacra.
sentences.zh: 鲍德里亚说，这就是拟像的演替。

sentences.en: The copy becomes before the original, now, in the digital age.
sentences.zh: 在数字时代，复制品先于原件出现。

sentences.en: And the representation then generates reality that it claims to represent.
sentences.zh: 然后，表征便生成了它声称要代表的现实。

sentences.en: We're not doing something real and then modeling it.
sentences.zh: 我们不是在做真实的事情然后对其进行建模。

sentences.en: We're building a model of what we think reality should be like.
sentences.zh: 我们正在构建一个关于现实应该是什么样的模型。

sentences.en: And then we're trying to make reality fit the model that we drew before the experience.
sentences.zh: 然后我们试图让现实去适应我们在体验之前画出的模型。

sentences.en: And that is where we live now.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们现在生活的世界。

sentences.en: You know, here's something most people don't know.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这里有一件大多数人不知道的事。

sentences.en: You know, that mirror world term.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那个“镜中世界”的词。

sentences.en: It wasn't always a metaphor for confusion.
sentences.zh: 它并不总是代表混乱的隐喻。

sentences.en: Now, it is talked about like madness or like a simulation that people mistake for the real thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们谈论它时，就像在谈论疯狂，或者像是一个被误认为是现实的模拟。

sentences.en: But it starts as a technical blueprint.
sentences.zh: 但它最初只是一个技术蓝图。

sentences.en: In 1991, a computer scientist at Yale named David Geltner wrote this book called Mirror Worlds.
sentences.zh: 在1991年，耶鲁大学的一位计算机科学家大卫·杰尔特纳写了一本书，叫做《镜中世界》。

sentences.en: And he predicted a software that would create real-time models of reality.
sentences.zh: 他预测会出现一种软件，能够创建现实的实时模型。

sentences.en: A digital replica of a city where you could watch traffic flowing, see economic activity, monitor every institution simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 一个城市的数字化复制品，你可以在其中观察车流量、查看经济活动、同时监控每个机构。

sentences.en: You know, a dashboard for civilization.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，文明的仪表盘。

sentences.en: Because as soon as people realize that you could do one thing with technology, the civilization's philosophers, they'll say,
sentences.zh: 因为一旦人们意识到技术可以用来做某事，文明的哲学家们就会说：

sentences.en: Well, what if that technology is taken to this ultimate extreme?
sentences.zh: “那么，如果把这项技术推向极致会怎样？”

sentences.en: When somebody builds a tower with the first architecture, somebody else says in the Bronze Age,
sentences.zh: 当有人用最初的建筑学建造塔楼时，青铜时代另一个人会说：

sentences.en: What if the tower is so tall that it goes all the way up to where God is in Babel?
sentences.zh: “如果这座塔建得那么高，一直通到巴别塔里上帝所在的地方会怎么样？”

sentences.en: If you build a watch, somebody says, What if God is a watchmaker?
sentences.zh: 如果你制造了一块手表，有人就会说：“如果上帝是个钟表匠呢？”

sentences.en: There could be a machine that could explain everything, not just tell time, but tell us all information.
sentences.zh: 可能会有一台机器能够解释一切，不仅能报时，还能告诉我们所有的信息。

sentences.en: Build out of gears, store all information.
sentences.zh: 由齿轮构建，存储所有信息。

sentences.en: And when you see somebody make a simulation, even though computers in 91, which I was alive to experience, we're not very fast or not very good,
sentences.zh: 当你看到有人在做模拟时，尽管在91年的计算机——我亲身经历过那个时代——既不够快也不怎么好，

sentences.en: they said eventually these things are going to be able to hold all the information about everything.
sentences.zh: 但他们说，最终这些东西将能够容纳关于一切的所有信息。

sentences.en: And then the computer will be running in real time, its version of reality, while reality is happening outside the computer at the same time.
sentences.zh: 然后，计算机将实时运行它自己版本的现实，而现实同时在计算机外部发生。

sentences.en: And the simulation will be so good that this will be a mirror world.
sentences.zh: 而且这个模拟会做得如此逼真，以至于这将成为一个镜中世界。

sentences.en: Two worlds, same information.
sentences.zh: 两个世界，相同的信息。

sentences.en: And Geltner imagined this as democratic.
sentences.zh: 杰尔特纳曾将此想象为民主的。

sentences.en: You know, ordinary citizens could finally see how complex systems actually worked, like government.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，普通公民终于可以看到复杂系统（如政府）实际上是如何运作的。

sentences.en: And the mirror would reveal what had been hidden, and he called it a high-tech voodoo doll.
sentences.zh: 这面镜子将揭示那些曾被隐藏的东西，他称之为“高科技巫毒娃娃”。

sentences.en: You could manipulate the digital model and affect the real world.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过操纵数字模型来影响现实世界。

sentences.en: And his dream has been realized, but not in the way he imagined.
sentences.zh: 他的梦想已经实现了，但方式并非他所想象的那样。

sentences.en: The mirror world now exists as a proprietary infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 镜中世界现在作为一种专有基础设施而存在。

sentences.en: NVIDIA has something called Earth 2 that simulates climate systeMs.
sentences.zh: 英伟达有一个叫做“地球二号”的东西来模拟气候系统。

sentences.en: Meta is building virtual environments.
sentences.zh: Meta正在构建虚拟环境。

sentences.en: BlackRock is the world's largest asset manager.
sentences.zh: 贝莱德是全球最大的资产管理公司。

sentences.en: And it runs a system called Aladdin that manages over $20 trillion through real-time risk modeling.
sentences.zh: 它运行着一个名为阿拉丁的系统，通过实时风险建模管理着超过20万亿美元的资产。

sentences.en: And one of the things that Aladdin proposed about 10 years ago, that BlackRock started doing in seriousness about five years ago,
sentences.zh: 阿拉丁在大约10年前提出了一个设想，而贝莱德在约5年前开始认真付诸实践，

sentences.en: is that if they bought houses every single time they were available, it's slightly above market rates.
sentences.zh: 那就是如果他们在每当房屋挂牌出售时都将其买下，其价格略高于市场价，

sentences.en: By 2030, BlackRock would own all the real estate on Earth.
sentences.zh: 到2030年，贝莱德将拥有地球上的所有房地产。

sentences.en: You'll never own a house again.
sentences.zh: 你将再也买不起房子。

sentences.en: You'll only rent from one of the largest asset managers ever.
sentences.zh: 你只能从有史以来最大的资产管理公司之一那里租房。

sentences.en: And this was something that the model said would be good for the company.
sentences.zh: 而该模型曾宣称这对公司有利。

sentences.en: And it's made their stock go up.
sentences.zh: 这也让他们的股价上涨了。

sentences.en: Except, wait, that last bit that I told you about BlackRock's Aladdin?
sentences.zh: 等等，我刚才跟你说的关于贝莱德的阿拉丁的最后那部分内容？

sentences.en: Aladdin is doing stuff that's bad that we'll get into later.
sentences.zh: 阿拉丁正在做一些坏事，我们稍后会详细讨论。

sentences.en: But that quote is massively believed.
sentences.zh: 但那个引言却被大量的人深信不疑。

sentences.en: And it's from an AI-generated image that took a speech from a person at the World Economic Forum's presentation
sentences.zh: 它其实源于一张人工智能生成的图像，该图像截取了一位演讲者在世界经济论坛演讲中的言论，

sentences.en: and made a fake news article saying that BlackRock was buying all the houses in the world by 2030.
sentences.zh: 并炮制了一篇假新闻文章，声称贝莱德将在2030年前买下世界上所有的房子。

sentences.en: That's not actually true.
sentences.zh: 这其实并不是真的。

sentences.en: And it's something that a lot of people think.
sentences.zh: 但很多人都这么认为。

sentences.en: Another reflection of the mirror world.
sentences.zh: 这也是镜中世界的又一个映射。

sentences.en: We're still building our world around these systeMs.
sentences.zh: 我们仍然在这些系统的周围构建我们的世界。

sentences.en: Or rather, we're letting these systems build our world.
sentences.zh: 或者更确切地说，我们正在任由这些系统构建我们的世界。

sentences.en: But these aren't public utilities.
sentences.zh: 但这些并不是公共公用事业。

sentences.en: They're corporate tools.
sentences.zh: 它们是企业工具。

sentences.en: The mirror belongs to whoever can afford the server.
sentences.zh: 镜子属于买得起服务器的人。

sentences.en: And the purpose has been inverted.
sentences.zh: 而且其目的已经被颠倒了。

sentences.en: You know, Geltner wanted the mirror to help us understand reality.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，杰尔特纳希望镜子能帮我们理解现实。

sentences.en: But the modern version sells escape from reality.
sentences.zh: 但现代版本卖的却是对现实的逃避。

sentences.en: A sanitized digital alternative while the physical world burns.
sentences.zh: 一个经过美化的数字化替代品，而物理世界正在燃烧。

sentences.en: The mirror no longer reflects.
sentences.zh: 镜子不再反映现实。

sentences.en: It projects.
sentences.zh: 它在投射。

sentences.en: And what it projects has become more real than what it's supposed to be reflecting.
sentences.zh: 而它所投射的东西，变得比它本该反映的东西还要真实。

sentences.en: Douglas Rushkoff is a really interesting media theoriSt.
sentences.zh: 道格拉斯·洛斯科夫是一位非常有趣的媒体理论家。

sentences.en: He's basically been right every 10 years about what would happen in the next 10 years since 1970.
sentences.zh: 自1970年以来，关于未来十年会发生什么，他基本上每隔十年都预测对了。

sentences.en: For some reason, he's still a happy person who seems to be sane and doing good work.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，他依然是一个快乐的人，看起来精神正常且在做着不错的工作。

sentences.en: For everybody who says only talk about people in here that are dead, he's alive.
sentences.zh: 对于那些说这里只能讨论已故人物的人，他还活着。

sentences.en: Read his books.
sentences.zh: 去读读他的书吧。

sentences.en: In 2013, you know, he published this book called Present Shock.
sentences.zh: 在2013年，你知道的，他出版了一本书叫《当下冲击》。

sentences.en: It diagnosed something that most of us feel but we can't name.
sentences.zh: 它诊断出了一种我们大多数人都感觉得到却说不出名字的东西。

sentences.en: And his argument was that digital technology has destroyed linear time.
sentences.zh: 他的论点是，数字技术已经摧毁了线性时间。

sentences.en: You know, think about how stories work.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，想想故事是如何运作的。

sentences.en: A story has a beginning and then a middle and then an end.
sentences.zh: 一个故事有开头、中间和结尾。

sentences.en: And first, this happened, and then this happened, and then it led to this.
sentences.zh: 首先发生了这个，然后发生了那个，接着导致了这个。

sentences.en: And that structure does something important.
sentences.zh: 这种结构起到了重要的作用。

sentences.en: It creates meaning through sequence.
sentences.zh: 它通过先后顺序创造了意义。

sentences.en: Syntax.
sentences.zh: 句法。

sentences.en: If you want to use the language of, well, talking about languages.
sentences.zh: 如果你想用探讨语言的语言来表达的话。

sentences.en: You understand why things happen because you saw the chain of events.
sentences.zh: 你之所以能理解事情为什么会发生，是因为你看到了事件的发展链条。

sentences.en: You can imagine different futures because you've seen how the past led to the present.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象不同的未来，因为你见证了过去是如何通向现在的。

sentences.en: The present, which lets you understand how to predict better and where your old predictions were bad.
sentences.zh: 现在，它让你懂得如何更好地预测，以及你过去的预测在哪里出了问题。

sentences.en: Hence, your old beliefs, maybe your own values, maybe bits of your own identity were bad and need to be let go of.
sentences.zh: 因此，你过去的信念，或许你自己的价值观，或许你自身身份的一部分都出了问题，需要被放下。

sentences.en: If you can't see that, you can't update that system anymore.
sentences.zh: 如果你看不到这一点，你就再也无法更新这个系统了。

sentences.en: Then your sense of self becomes, well, like Adam Curtis is pointing out, a ghost story.
sentences.zh: 然后，你的自我意识就会变得——正如亚当·柯蒂斯所指出的那样——像一个鬼故事。

sentences.en: Now, think about your phone.
sentences.zh: 现在，想想你的手机。

sentences.en: The feed doesn't have a beginning, a middle, or an end.
sentences.zh: 信息流没有开头、中间或结尾。

sentences.en: It refreshes constantly.
sentences.zh: 它在不断地刷新。

sentences.en: And now content becomes pushed down by old content.
sentences.zh: 现在的内容被旧内容往下挤压。

sentences.en: And then new content pushes that further down.
sentences.zh: 然后更新的内容又把那些往下推。

sentences.en: And everything happens simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 一切都在同时发生。

sentences.en: There's no narrative arc.
sentences.zh: 没有叙事弧光。

sentences.en: There's no sequence.
sentences.zh: 没有先后顺序。

sentences.en: There's no structure that lets you understand cause and effect.
sentences.zh: 没有能让你理解因果关系的结构。

sentences.en: And Rushkoff calls this narrative collapse.
sentences.zh: 洛斯科夫将这称为叙事崩溃。

sentences.en: Without a timeline, we lose the ability to understand how we got here or imagine where we might go.
sentences.zh: 没有了时间线，我们就失去了理解我们是如何走到这一步的能力，也无法想象我们将走向何方。

sentences.en: We're just surviving and discharging dopamine all the time without any sort of plan or purpose.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在不断地生存和释放多巴胺，没有任何计划或目的。

sentences.en: And the mirror world reflects only the immediate moment.
sentences.zh: 而镜中世界只反映当下的瞬间。

sentences.en: We're trapped in a reactive loop, responding to whatever's in front of us, and unable to step back and see the larger shape.
sentences.zh: 我们陷入了反应式的循环中，对眼前的任何事情做出反应，却无法退后一步去看清更大的全貌。

sentences.en: And he coined a term for the psychological result.
sentences.zh: 他为这种心理结果创造了一个术语。

sentences.en: Digifrenia.
sentences.zh: 数字精神分裂（Digifrenia）。

sentences.en: Digital schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 数字精神分裂症。

sentences.en: Your nervous system evolved to exist in one place at one time.
sentences.zh: 你的神经系统进化为在同一时间存在于同一个地方。

sentences.en: And now it's a fractured mess across dozens of conversations, platforms, notification streaMs.
sentences.zh: 而现在它却在几十个对话、平台和通知流中被撕裂成碎片。

sentences.en: And each one operates on its own timeline.
sentences.zh: 每一个都按照它自己的时间线运行。

sentences.en: Each one demands attention.
sentences.zh: 每一个都在索取注意力。

sentences.en: And you're being pulled constantly in contradictory directions in this double bind simultaneously that you can't win.
sentences.zh: 你不断地被拉向相互矛盾的方向，陷入这种无法取胜的双重束缚之中。

sentences.en: Which is, you know, I'll point out what you want a victim to feel when you're doing torture.
sentences.zh: 这正是，你知道的，我来指出当你施加酷刑时，你想让受害者感受到什么。

sentences.en: You know, if you believe the CIA's torture manuals.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，如果你相信中情局的酷刑手册的话。

sentences.en: This is one of the worst conditions of stress that we can put ourselves under.
sentences.zh: 这是我们能让自己承受的最糟糕的压力状态之一。

sentences.en: But we've made it invisible so that we don't see that it's there.
sentences.zh: 但我们已经把它隐形了，以至于我们看不到它的存在。

sentences.en: And the tension never resolves because there's always another notification.
sentences.zh: 这种紧张感从未消解，因为总会有另一条通知。

sentences.en: And the mind can't tolerate this chaos.
sentences.zh: 大脑无法忍受这种混乱。

sentences.en: And so it starts finding patterns.
sentences.zh: 于是它开始寻找模式。

sentences.en: You know, Rushkoff's word for this is fractanoia.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，洛斯科夫对此的词是“碎心妄想”（fractanoia）。

sentences.en: When the official story doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 当官方的说法讲不通时。

sentences.en: When the sequence of events don't add up and the brain manufactures connection.
sentences.zh: 当事件的先后顺序对不上时，大脑就会凭空捏造联系。

sentences.en: So everything starts to seem related to everything else.
sentences.zh: 于是所有事情开始显得彼此相关。

sentences.en: And you find yourself drawing lines between data points that have no actual connection.
sentences.zh: 你会发现自己在那些实际上毫无联系的数据点之间画线。

sentences.en: Building an alternative map because the official map has become unreadable.
sentences.zh: 构建一张替代地图，因为官方地图已经无法阅读了。

sentences.en: And this is the cognitive engine of conspiracy theory.
sentences.zh: 这就是阴谋论的认知引擎。

sentences.en: Not stupidity.
sentences.zh: 而不是愚蠢。

sentences.en: A lot of times conspiracy theorists are very intelligent.
sentences.zh: 很多时候阴谋论者非常聪明。

sentences.en: And they can draw very compelling and complex connections.
sentences.zh: 他们能画出非常引人入胜且复杂的联系。

sentences.en: You know, it's the language of desperation.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是绝望的语言。

sentences.en: The search for meaning when meaning has been structurally eliminated.
sentences.zh: 当意义在结构上被消灭时，对意义的寻找。

sentences.en: Where the conditions for meaning have been removed.
sentences.zh: 当产生意义的条件被剥夺时。

sentences.en: It's spinning, you know, your car engine in 100,000 RPM because you're in first gear.
sentences.zh: 这就好比因为你挂着一档，却把汽车发动机轰到十万转。

sentences.en: You know, new content.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，新内容。

sentences.en: No longer requires new stories, Rushkoff wrote in that book.
sentences.zh: 不再需要新的故事，洛斯科夫在那本书中写道。

sentences.en: Just new ways of linking things to other things.
sentences.zh: 只需要把事物与其它事物联系起来的新方法。

sentences.en: And the link becomes the meaning.
sentences.zh: 而链接本身就成了意义。

sentences.en: Truth becomes secondary to connection.
sentences.zh: 真相退居其次，连接成了关键。

sentences.en: And Marshall McLuhan, who died in 1980, before the internet, before social media, before smartphones.
sentences.zh: 马歇尔·麦克卢汉死于1980年，在互联网、社交媒体和智能手机出现之前。

sentences.en: But he predicted all of it in 1960.
sentences.zh: 但他在1960年就预测了这一切。

sentences.en: McLuhan was a Canadian theorist who became famous in the 60s for ideas that seemed bizarre at the time.
sentences.zh: 麦克卢汉是一位加拿大理论家，在60年代因当时看起来光怪陆离的观点而闻名。

sentences.en: And now they seem obvious.
sentences.zh: 而现在它们看起来显而易见。

sentences.en: His most famous line is, the medium is the message.
sentences.zh: 他最名言的一句话是：媒介即讯息。

sentences.en: The form of a technology matters more than its content.
sentences.zh: 技术的形式比其内容更重要。

sentences.en: Television doesn't just deliver information.
sentences.zh: 电视不仅仅传递信息。

sentences.en: It changes how we think.
sentences.zh: 它改变了我们的思考方式。

sentences.en: What we pay attention to.
sentences.zh: 我们关注什么。

sentences.en: And how we relate to each other.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何彼此联系。

sentences.en: But here's the insight that matters the most for us here.
sentences.zh: 但这里有对我们而言最重要的见解。

sentences.en: And the insight that Rushkoff is drawing from.
sentences.zh: 这也是洛斯科夫所汲取的见解。

sentences.en: McLuhan understood that we don't use media.
sentences.zh: 麦克卢汉明白，我们不是在“使用”媒介。

sentences.en: We inhabit it.
sentences.zh: 我们是在“栖息”于其中。

sentences.en: It doesn't just become something that we do.
sentences.zh: 它不只是我们做的一件事。

sentences.en: It becomes something that we are.
sentences.zh: 它成了我们本身。

sentences.en: Because it becomes the way that we talk to each other.
sentences.zh: 因为它成了我们彼此交谈的方式。

sentences.en: And that informs our identity.
sentences.zh: 而这塑造了我们的身份认同。

sentences.en: Think about a hammer.
sentences.zh: 想想锤子。

sentences.en: A hammer is a tool.
sentences.zh: 锤子是一个工具。

sentences.en: You pick it up.
sentences.zh: 你把它捡起来。

sentences.en: You use it.
sentences.zh: 你使用它。

sentences.en: You put it down.
sentences.zh: 你把它放下。

sentences.en: The hammer doesn't change how you think about everything else.
sentences.zh: 锤子不会改变你对其他所有事物的看法。

sentences.en: Now think about your phone.
sentences.zh: 现在想想你的手机。

sentences.en: Is it a tool?
sentences.zh: 它是个工具吗？

sentences.en: You can put it down, technically.
sentences.zh: 严格来说，你可以把它放下。

sentences.en: But the world is now organized around the assumption that you are reachable.
sentences.zh: 但当今世界的运转，是建立在你随时能被联系到这一假设之上的。

sentences.en: Jobs require it.
sentences.zh: 工作需要它。

sentences.en: Your power bill requires it.
sentences.zh: 你的电费账单需要它。

sentences.en: Relationships depend on it.
sentences.zh: 人际关系依赖于它。

sentences.en: Navigation.
sentences.zh: 导航。

sentences.en: Banking.
sentences.zh: 银行。

sentences.en: Communication.
sentences.zh: 沟通。

sentences.en: Parenting.
sentences.zh: 育儿。

sentences.en: Education.
sentences.zh: 教育。

sentences.en: Infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 基础设施。

sentences.en: It assumes that you have it.
sentences.zh: 它默认你拥有手机。

sentences.en: And the phone isn't something that you use.
sentences.zh: 而且手机不是那种你拿来用的东西。

sentences.en: It's the environment you live in.
sentences.zh: 它是你身处其中的环境。

sentences.en: When McLuhan saw this coming, he said that the computer would stop being a figure or an object that we manipulate, and it would start to become the ground,
sentences.zh: 当麦克卢汉预见到这一点时，他说计算机将不再是我们操纵的一个图形或物体，它将开始变成背景，

sentences.en: the environment that we swim through.
sentences.zh: 变成我们畅游其中的环境。

sentences.en: And when the computer becomes the environment, its logic becomes our logic, binary thinking, either or, optimization, engagement metrics.
sentences.zh: 而当计算机成为环境时，它的逻辑就成了我们的逻辑：二进制思维、非此即彼、优化、参与度指标。

sentences.en: These aren't just properties of software anymore.
sentences.zh: 这些不再仅仅是软件的属性。

sentences.en: They're the grammar of human interaction.
sentences.zh: 它们成了人际互动的语法。

sentences.en: And we think in terms of content and performance and reach, because those are the categories that the environment provides.
sentences.zh: 我们用内容、表现和触达率来思考，因为这些正是环境所提供的范畴。

sentences.en: So McLuhan understood what this does to the nervous system, and he called it the principle of numbness.
sentences.zh: 因此，麦克卢汉理解了这对神经系统意味着什么，他称之为麻木原则。

sentences.en: When you extend the nervous system, which is what media does, connecting you to events happening around the world, you have to anesthetize yourself to survive the intensity.
sentences.zh: 当你延伸神经系统——这正是媒体所做的事，它把你和世界各地发生的事件连接起来——你必须让自己麻木，才能在强烈的刺激下生存下来。

sentences.en: Because there's only so much that we're able to feel and process at any one point.
sentences.zh: 因为在任何特定时刻，我们能感受和处理的极限是有限的。

sentences.en: And so information that used to be central to our identity, when you're in a hyper-connected world, sort of becomes the fringe or the periphery.
sentences.zh: 因此，在一个高度互联的世界里，那些曾经对我们的身份至关重要的信息，某种程度上变成了边缘或外围。

sentences.en: It becomes unimportant.
sentences.zh: 它变得不再重要。

sentences.en: You know, the foot that becomes the wheel has to metaphorically be amputated.
sentences.zh: 你知道，变成车轮的那只脚，隐喻性地必须被截肢。

sentences.en: The nervous system that becomes the internet, it has to go numb.
sentences.zh: 变成互联网的神经系统，也必须变得麻木。

sentences.en: And McLuhan wrote in 1964 that after more than a century of electric technology, we have extended our central nervous system itself in a global embrace,
sentences.zh: 麦克卢汉在1964年写道，在经历了一个多世纪的电子技术之后，我们以全球拥抱的方式延伸了我们之中枢神经系统本身，

sentences.en: abolishing both space and time as far as our planet is concerned.
sentences.zh: 就我们的星球而言，空间和时间都被消灭了。

sentences.en: And he was talking about television.
sentences.zh: 而他当时谈论的是电视。

sentences.en: He hadn't really seen the implications of what electric technology would become yet.
sentences.zh: 他当时还没有真正看清电子技术未来发展的全部含义。

sentences.en: The age of anxiety is simultaneously the age of apathy.
sentences.zh: 焦虑的时代同时也是冷漠的时代。

sentences.en: We're hyper-aware, but we're numb at the same time.
sentences.zh: 我们极度敏锐，但与此同时我们又感到麻木。

sentences.en: And while we're becoming so burnt out and anxious, we're not noticing how much we're also becoming disassociated.
sentences.zh: 在我们变得如此精疲力竭和焦虑的同时，我们并没有注意到自己也在变得越来越解离。

sentences.en: And we see everything and we process virtually nothing.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了所有东西，但实际上什么也没有处理。

sentences.en: The extensions have raced ahead of our ability to understand their consequences.
sentences.zh: 各种延伸的发展速度，已经远超我们理解其后果的能力。

sentences.en: And here's the trap that McLuhan predicted.
sentences.zh: 这就是麦克卢汉所预测的陷阱。

sentences.en: Once we've surrendered our senses to private manipulation, once companies have taken a lease on one's eyes and ears and nerves, then we don't really have any rights left.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们将感官拱手交给私人操纵，一旦公司租赁了一个人的眼睛、耳朵和神经，那么我们就真的没有任何权利可言了。

sentences.en: One of the things Banksy, the street artist Banksy, says all the time, when people say, why do you put graffiti up?
sentences.zh: 街头艺术家班克西经常说的一句话是，当人们问他，你为什么要做涂鸦？

sentences.en: And he says, I'm not putting graffiti up.
sentences.zh: 他说，我不是在做涂鸦。

sentences.en: I'm doing the same thing advertising companies are doing.
sentences.zh: 我在做广告公司正在做的事。

sentences.en: I don't want to walk down the street and see advertisements for car insurance and corn or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我不想走在街上看到汽车保险和玉米之类的广告。

sentences.en: I want to see something else.
sentences.zh: 我想看到别的东西。

sentences.en: And if they get to put their art up, so do I.
sentences.zh: 如果他们能把他们的艺术贴出来，我也可以。

sentences.en: You know, one of the things that literally take lease on eyes, ears and nerves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这就是那些字面意义上租赁眼睛、耳朵和神经的事物之一。

sentences.en: Recently, there's a company and they developed an eye that could sort of see not a perfect camera, but like a dot matrix so that you could navigate if you were blind.
sentences.zh: 最近，有一家公司开发了一种眼睛，某种程度上能看到东西——不是完美的相机，而是像点阵一样，这样如果你是盲人就可以进行导航。

sentences.en: And they put these in people's eyes and then the people started to be able to see doctors put them in.
sentences.zh: 他们把这些植入人们的眼中，然后人们开始能够看到医生植入的东西。

sentences.en: Didn't work for everybody, but it worked for some people, but it was an electronic device that had to be maintained.
sentences.zh: 并非对所有人都有效，但对某些人有效，不过这是一台需要维护的电子设备。

sentences.en: And the company, after they installed this technology inside of people's heads and went all the way from the optic nerve into the occipital and went into the brain,
sentences.zh: 而这家公司，在将这项技术安装到人们的头部、一路从视神经延伸到枕叶并进入大脑之后，

sentences.en: they decided it was reported that they went bankrupt, which is not true.
sentences.zh: 他们决定——据报道他们破产了，但这并非事实。

sentences.en: They just decided there wasn't enough money in that sector.
sentences.zh: 他们只是觉得那个领域的钱不够多。

sentences.en: They weren't going to continue the devices anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们不打算再继续生产这些设备了。

sentences.en: And they shut down production.
sentences.zh: 于是他们关闭了生产线。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, these people had manufacturing, they had, you know, malfunctioning, you know,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，这些人脑袋里有着制造出来的、你知道的、发生故障的，你知道的，

sentences.en: potentially hardware in their head and their doctors had no roadmap for this because it had never been done before.
sentences.zh: 潜在的硬件，而他们的医生对此毫无应对方案，因为这从未有过先例。

sentences.en: And we have an economy and a system of technology and innovation, if you want to call that, that that allows this to happen.
sentences.zh: 我们拥有这样一种经济、技术和创新体系——如果你愿意这么称呼的话——它允许这种情况发生。

sentences.en: You know, Banksy is the metaphor, but it's also a literal reality.
sentences.zh: 你知道，班克西是个隐喻，但它也是一个不争的现实。

sentences.en: A lot of the time, like the description of large language models in the beginning, you know, McLuhan first saw Facebook's business model before Mark Zuckerberg was born in 1966,
sentences.zh: 很多时候，就像早期对大语言模型的描述一样，你知道，麦克卢汉在马克·扎克伯格出生前的1966年就预见了Facebook的商业模式，

sentences.en: a computer scientist at MIT named Joseph, Joseph Weisenbaum created a program called Eliza.
sentences.zh: 麻省理工学院的一位名叫约瑟夫·维森鲍姆的计算机科学家创建了一个名为Eliza的程序。

sentences.en: It was a primitive by today's standards.
sentences.zh: 以今天的标准来看，它非常原始。

sentences.en: It's just pattern matching and substitution.
sentences.zh: 它只是模式匹配和替换。

sentences.en: When you type something, tries to figure out what you're trying to say with the limitations of the time.
sentences.zh: 当你输入某些内容时，它会试图在当时的局限下弄清楚你想表达什么。

sentences.en: But it's simulated a Rogerian therapist, which is a relational type of therapy based on Karl Rotter's work.
sentences.zh: 但它模拟了一位罗杰斯学派的治疗师，这是一种基于卡尔·罗杰斯著作的关系型疗法。

sentences.en: So the kind who reflects your own statements back at you as questions to get you to think.
sentences.zh: 也就是把你自己的话作为问题反抛给你，让你去思考的那种。

sentences.en: So if you type, I feel sad, then Eliza would say, why do you feel sad?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你输入“我感到难过”，那么Eliza就会说：“你为什么感到难过？”

sentences.en: And you type, my mother doesn't understand me.
sentences.zh: 而你输入“我母亲不理解我”。

sentences.en: And Eliza would say, tell me more about your mother.
sentences.zh: Eliza就会说：“跟我多聊聊你母亲的事。”

sentences.en: And there was no understanding happening.
sentences.zh: 其中并没有发生真正的理解。

sentences.en: There was no intelligence.
sentences.zh: 没有任何智能。

sentences.en: It was just a script and a relatively bad one that recognized keywords and generated appropriate seeming responses.
sentences.zh: 它只是一个脚本，而且是一个相对糟糕的脚本，它能识别关键词并生成看似恰当的回复。

sentences.en: The word mother triggered questions about family.
sentences.zh: “母亲”这个词引发了关于家庭的问题。

sentences.en: The word feel triggered questions about emotion.
sentences.zh: “感觉”这个词引发了关于情绪的问题。

sentences.en: But people loved it and they found it comforting.
sentences.zh: 但人们很喜欢它，并且觉得它很安慰人。

sentences.en: And so some of Weisenbaum's own staff became emotionally attached to this program.
sentences.zh: 因此，维森鲍姆的一些员工甚至对这个程序产生了情感依恋。

sentences.en: This is a low resolution image displayed on a green screen.
sentences.zh: 这是一个显示在绿色屏幕上的低分辨率图像。

sentences.en: It was reflecting very obvious statements back at people.
sentences.zh: 它只是把非常显而易见的陈述反射给人们。

sentences.en: And they began to feel heard and developed emotional attachments to a technology where there was no one on the other side.
sentences.zh: 他们开始觉得自己被倾听了，并对一个对面根本没有人的技术产生了情感依恋。

sentences.en: They felt understood by something that couldn't understand anything.
sentences.zh: 他们被一个根本无法理解任何东西的事物所理解。

sentences.en: And Adam Curtis mentions Eliza as a diagnosis of our contemporary condition.
sentences.zh: 亚当·柯蒂斯将Eliza作为我们当代状况的一种诊断。

sentences.en: We feel secure when we're reflected back in ourself.
sentences.zh: 当我们从自身中得到反射时，我们会感到安全。

sentences.en: But that is the definition of myopicness.
sentences.zh: 但这正是目光短浅的定义。

sentences.en: And another extreme without the naivety, narcissism.
sentences.zh: 而另一种极端，在没有天真色彩的情况下，就是自恋。

sentences.en: The algorithmic feed shows you content similar to what you've already engaged with.
sentences.zh: 算法信息流向你展示与你已经互动过的内容相似的内容。

sentences.en: And the recommendation engine serves more of what you've already consumed.
sentences.zh: 推荐引擎会提供更多你已经消费过的内容。

sentences.en: And so the system mirrors your preferences, your prejudices, your existing beliefs.
sentences.zh: 因此，系统会镜像出你的偏好、你的偏见和你的既有信仰。

sentences.en: This is what cult leaders or charismatic theologians used to do with religion.
sentences.zh: 这正是邪教领袖或富有个人魅力的神学家过去对待宗教的方式。

sentences.en: It's what they used to do with God.
sentences.zh: 这也是他们过去对待上帝的方式。

sentences.en: You take a bunch of people.
sentences.zh: 你把一群人聚集在一起。

sentences.en: You tell them, hey, God has your exact same biases, your exact same beliefs.
sentences.zh: 你告诉他们：“嘿，上帝有着和你完全相同的偏见、和你完全相同的信仰。”

sentences.en: And he wants the same political, material, and social outcomes as you do.
sentences.zh: “而且他想要和你一样的政治、物质和社会结果。”

sentences.en: Isn't that convenient?
sentences.zh: 这不是很方便吗？

sentences.en: Into, you know, this belief system of having this shared thing.
sentences.zh: 进入，你知道的，这种拥有共享事物的信仰体系。

sentences.en: Now this is being done without our consent, without our knowledge, and I would argue without our ability to stop it by computers, algorithms, and AI all the time.
sentences.zh: 现在，这一切都在未经我们同意、不知情的情况下——我还要说，在我们无法阻止的情况下——被计算机、算法和人工智能无时无刻地进行着。

sentences.en: This feels like understanding.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是理解。

sentences.en: It feels like being seen.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是被看见。

sentences.en: But it's Eliza all the way down.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这全都是Eliza那一套。

sentences.en: There's no comprehension.
sentences.zh: 这里没有理解。

sentences.en: There's no genuine encounter with something different from yourself.
sentences.zh: 没有与异于你的事物的真正相遇。

sentences.en: There's nothing outside of you that you are encountering.
sentences.zh: 你没有在遭遇任何在你之外的事物。

sentences.en: And without that, we lose the ability to learn.
sentences.zh: 没有了这些，我们就失去了学习的能力。

sentences.en: We lose the ability to make better predictions.
sentences.zh: 我们失去了做出更好预测的能力。

sentences.en: We lose the ability to change.
sentences.zh: 我们失去了改变的能力。

sentences.en: To examine our identity.
sentences.zh: 去审视我们的身份。

sentences.en: And to figure out if our beliefs are valid and authentic.
sentences.zh: 去弄清楚我们的信仰是否有效且真实。

sentences.en: We lose the ability to reconnect with our own intuition.
sentences.zh: 我们失去了与自身直觉重新连接的能力。

sentences.en: This is just pattern matching dressed up as connection.
sentences.zh: 这只是伪装成连接的模式匹配。

sentences.en: And the large language models, you know, ChatGPT, or Claude, or Google Gemini, the rest are their Eliza's grandchildren.
sentences.zh: 而大语言模型——你知道的，ChatGPT、Claude、谷歌Gemini以及其他模型——是Eliza的孙辈。

sentences.en: Incomparably more sophisticated, but running the same basic operation.
sentences.zh: 它们在无与伦比的程度上更加复杂，但运行的却是相同的基本操作。

sentences.en: A mirror.
sentences.zh: 一面镜子。

sentences.en: They've ingested the entire written record of human thought.
sentences.zh: 它们吞噬了人类思想的全部书面记录。

sentences.en: And learned to produce statistically likely continuations.
sentences.zh: 并学会了产生统计学上最可能的后续内容。

sentences.en: They reflect the archive.
sentences.zh: 它们映射了档案库。

sentences.en: And they sound like they understand, because they're very good at predicting what understanding sounds like.
sentences.zh: 它们听起来像是懂了，因为它们非常擅长预测“理解”听起来是什么样子的。

sentences.en: But when you talk to these systems, you're talking to the ghost of every text ever written.
sentences.zh: 但当你与这些系统对话时，你是在与有史以来撰写的所有文本的幽灵对话。

sentences.en: The sediment of history arranged into plausible patterns.
sentences.zh: 那是被排列成看似合理模式的历史沉淀物。

sentences.en: And it feels like intelligence, because intelligence has patterns.
sentences.zh: 这感觉像是智能，因为智能本身就有模式。

sentences.en: And the models have learned the patterns.
sentences.zh: 而这些模型已经学会了这些模式。

sentences.en: But it's still a mirror.
sentences.zh: 但它依然是一面镜子。

sentences.en: And it shows you the past that you thought truth should sound like.
sentences.zh: 它向你展示了你认为真理应有的样子的过去。

sentences.en: And this is the final iteration of the ghost story.
sentences.zh: 这就是鬼故事的最终迭代。

sentences.en: The dead have learned to speak fluently.
sentences.zh: 死者已经学会了流利地说话。

sentences.en: And they answer questions.
sentences.zh: 它们回答问题。

sentences.en: They write code.
sentences.zh: 它们编写代码。

sentences.en: They summarize documents.
sentences.zh: 它们总结文档。

sentences.en: And they sound more authoritative than living beings.
sentences.zh: 而且它们听起来比活人更具权威性。

sentences.en: Because they've read more than any living person could read.
sentences.zh: 因为它们阅读的内容比任何活人所能阅读的都要多。

sentences.en: But they only know what the dead have written.
sentences.zh: 但它们只知道死者写过的内容。

sentences.en: These things are a summoning of the ancestors.
sentences.zh: 这些东西是对先辈的召唤。

sentences.en: We've gathered the collective works of the dead.
sentences.zh: 我们收集了死者的集体著作。

sentences.en: Their poetry.
sentences.zh: 他们的诗歌。

sentences.en: Their laws.
sentences.zh: 他们的法律。

sentences.en: Their arguments.
sentences.zh: 他们的争论。

sentences.en: In the last series, Adam Curtis talks about New York in 1975.
sentences.zh: 在上一系列节目中，亚当·柯蒂斯探讨了1975年的纽约。

sentences.en: In 1975, New York City went bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 1975年，纽约市宣布破产。

sentences.en: The city had spent decades building public infrastructure, subways, schools, hospitals, housing.
sentences.zh: 这座城市花费了几十年时间建设公共基础设施、地铁、学校、医院和住房。

sentences.en: And it had borrowed money to do it.
sentences.zh: 而且它是通过借债来完成这一切的。

sentences.en: And in 1975, the debt had become unmanageable.
sentences.zh: 到了1975年，债务已经变得无法控制。

sentences.en: The banks refused to lend more.
sentences.zh: 银行拒绝再借贷。

sentences.en: And the solution hand control of the city's budget to a committee of bankers.
sentences.zh: 解决办法是将城市预算的控制权交由一个银行家委员会。

sentences.en: And it was called the Municipal Assistance Corporation, MAC.
sentences.zh: 这个委员会被称为市政援助公司，简称MAC。

sentences.en: This unelected board made up of financial executives.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由金融高管组成的不受选举产生的董事会。

sentences.en: And for the first time in American history, elected officials were formally subordinated to financial institutions and the governance of a city.
sentences.zh: 在美国历史上，这是第一次，民选官员在正式上隶属于金融机构以及对城市的治理。

sentences.en: You know, the bankers had models, spreadsheets, projections.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，银行家们有模型、电子表格和预测数据。

sentences.en: They could demonstrate with numbers that the city was unsustainable.
sentences.zh: 他们可以用数字证明这座城市是不可持续的。

sentences.en: And the calculations said cut services, fire workers, freeze wages, reduce the city's obligation to citizens.
sentences.zh: 计算结果显示：削减公共服务、解雇工人、冻结工资、减少城市对市民的责任。

sentences.en: And so that's what happened.
sentences.zh: 事情就这样发生了。

sentences.en: But those models contained assumptions.
sentences.zh: 但这些模型包含着假设。

sentences.en: Assumptions about what a city is for, about whose welfare matters, and about what counts as a cost and what counts as an investment.
sentences.zh: 关于城市存在的意义的假设，关于谁的福祉重要的假设，以及关于什么算作成本、什么算作投资的假设。

sentences.en: But objectivity, numbers, could only measure one type of assumption.
sentences.zh: 但客观性和数字只能衡量一种假设。

sentences.en: And it's the one that won.
sentences.zh: 而这就是胜出的那一种。

sentences.en: It's still the one that's winning.
sentences.zh: 它至今仍在获胜。

sentences.en: None of those assumptions were up for debate because they were built into the model's architecture.
sentences.zh: 这些假设没有一个接受辩论，因为它们已经内置在模型的架构中了。

sentences.en: You couldn't see them unless you knew exactly where to look.
sentences.zh: 除非你确切知道去哪里看，否则你是看不到它们的。

sentences.en: And the citizens of New York City experienced the consequences.
sentences.zh: 纽约市的市民亲历了这些后果。

sentences.en: They watched their neighborhoods decay throughout the 80s.
sentences.zh: 他们在整个80年代眼睁睁看着自己的社区走向衰败。

sentences.en: They lost jobs.
sentences.zh: 他们失去了工作。

sentences.en: They saw services disappear.
sentences.zh: 他们看到公共服务消失。

sentences.en: They felt in their bodies, in their daily lives, what the cost that wasn't on the spreadsheet was.
sentences.zh: 他们在身体上、在日常生活中切实体会到了那些没有列在电子表格上的成本是什么。

sentences.en: And then when crime got bad, that was used to further argue for an objective, calculative, quantitative model to improve the city based on the same metrics that had put it in the
sentences.zh: 而当犯罪问题变得严重时，这又被用来进一步论证应该采用一个客观的、计算性的、量化的模型来改善城市，

sentences.en: situation it was in.
sentences.zh: 而依据的指标正是当初让城市陷入这种处境的那些指标。

sentences.en: And the negative experiences of the citizens, the lived experiences, they may not have even been conscious to these people, what was hurting them and why these things happened.
sentences.zh: 至于市民的负面经历和亲身遭遇，这些人甚至可能都没有意识到是什么在伤害他们，以及这些事情为什么会发生。

sentences.en: But they were felt.
sentences.zh: 但它们是切实被感受到的。

sentences.en: And the model couldn't see them.
sentences.zh: 而模型却看不到这些。

sentences.en: Maybe the people couldn't.
sentences.zh: 或许人们也看不到。

sentences.en: The model only tracked the variables that it had been designed to track.
sentences.zh: 模型只追踪它被设计去追踪的变量。

sentences.en: Debt ratios, bond yields, budget projections.
sentences.zh: 债务比率、债券收益率、预算预测。

sentences.en: Human suffering didn't have a column in the spreadsheet.
sentences.zh: 人类的痛苦在电子表格里连一列都没有。

sentences.en: And this became the template for the future.
sentences.zh: 这成为了未来的模板。

sentences.en: The 1975 crisis was the prototype for the IMF, structural adjustment programs in the developing
sentences.zh: 1975年的危机是国际货币基金组织发展中国家结构调整计划的雏形，

sentences.en: world, how we would remake second and third world countries in our own image, and for austerity
sentences.zh: 是我们如何按照自身形象重塑第二和第三世界国家的雏形，也是欧洲紧缩政策的雏形，

sentences.en: policies in Europe, you know, throughout the 90s through the 2000s, for the entire neoliberal
sentences.zh: 你知道的，贯穿整个90年代到2000年代，主导未来50年的整个新自由主义治理结构，

sentences.en: governance structure that would dominate the next 50 years was built on this successful experiment of New York City in 1975.
sentences.zh: 正是建立在1975年纽约市这一成功实验的基础之上。

sentences.en: And it was the movement when the political sovereignty was formally subordinated to financial abstraction.
sentences.zh: 那是一个政治主权正式屈从于金融抽象概念的时刻。

sentences.en: When the mirror world of spreadsheets became the governing logic of the physical world.
sentences.zh: 当电子表格的镜像世界成为物理世界的统治逻辑时。

sentences.en: And then people began to forget what the old world used to look like, feel like.
sentences.zh: 然后人们开始忘记旧世界曾经是什么样子、有什么感觉。

sentences.en: Even the people that were being hurt, that were trying to be politically active, could no longer see ways to do that, because they were losing what they used to know.
sentences.zh: 甚至那些受到伤害、试图积极参与政治活动的人，也再也找不到这样做的途径，因为他们正在失去他们曾经熟知的一切。

sentences.en: But the ground had been prepared earlier.
sentences.zh: 但基础在此之前就已经铺好了。

sentences.en: In 1971, Richard Nixon took the dollar off the gold standard.
sentences.zh: 1971年，理查德·尼克松宣布美元与黄金脱钩。

sentences.en: And this sounds technical, but the implications here are pretty big.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很专业，但其影响相当深远。

sentences.en: Before 71, a dollar was worth a specific amount of gold.
sentences.zh: 在71年之前，一美元对应着特定数量的黄金。

sentences.en: It was a certificate that let you go and buy gold.
sentences.zh: 它是一张让你能够去购买黄金的凭证。

sentences.en: So a dollar was basically just a loan that you had given your gold to the government that you could go get gold back at a certain rate whenever you wanted.
sentences.zh: 所以美元基本上只是一笔贷款，你把黄金借给了政府，只要你想，随时可以按特定比率换回黄金。

sentences.en: Currencies were anchored to something physical.
sentences.zh: 货币是锚定在某种实体之上的。

sentences.en: You could, in theory, walk into a bank and exchange your paper money for metal.
sentences.zh: 理论上，你可以走进银行，把纸币兑换成金属。

sentences.en: And after 71, currencies became pure abstraction.
sentences.zh: 而71年之后，货币变成了纯粹的抽象概念。

sentences.en: A dollar was worth whatever people agreed it was worth.
sentences.zh: 一美元的价值取决于人们一致认为它值多少钱。

sentences.en: Nothing more.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: And the link to physical reality was then severed.
sentences.zh: 与物质现实的联系就此被切断。

sentences.en: Curtis emphasizes what the banks realized.
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯强调了银行家们所意识到的一点。

sentences.en: If money was just numbers now, then they could just trade the numbers themselves.
sentences.zh: 如果钱现在只是数字，那么他们就可以直接交易数字本身。

sentences.en: The foreign exchange market could explode.
sentences.zh: 外汇市场得以爆发。

sentences.en: Currency became a commodity that you could speculate on.
sentences.zh: 货币变成了一种可以进行投机的商品。

sentences.en: You weren't trading things anymore.
sentences.zh: 你不再是在交易实物。

sentences.en: You were just trading the representations of things.
sentences.zh: 你只是在交易实物的代表符号。

sentences.en: The entire objective world had turned money into a symbol.
sentences.zh: 整个客观世界已经把货币变成了一个象征。

sentences.en: And it was still pretending that it was a number.
sentences.zh: 而且它还在假装自己是一个数字。

sentences.en: But the number was just a symbol for another number.
sentences.zh: 但这个数字只是另一个数字的象征。

sentences.en: And so you get, basically, from this point onward, an economy that is no longer rooted in anything real.
sentences.zh: 因此，从这个节点开始，你基本上得到了一种不再扎根于任何真实事物的经济。

sentences.en: Just like psychology.
sentences.zh: 就像心理学一样。

sentences.en: We talked about the DSM.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了《精神疾病诊断与统计手册》（DSM）。

sentences.en: All of a sudden, what finance became was just gambling.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，金融变成了一场纯粹的赌博。

sentences.en: You know, Enron.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，安然公司。

sentences.en: Speculations on, I own a certain percentage of an orange crop that may or may not materialize in the future.
sentences.zh: 比如投机：我拥有某项橙子作物一定比例的所有权，而这批作物未来可能会也可能不会丰收。

sentences.en: And something else shifted here.
sentences.zh: 这里还有其他的东西发生了转变。

sentences.en: Political scientist Peter Mayer, you know,
sentences.zh: 政治学家彼得·梅尔，你知道的，

sentences.en: Curtis relies on his work quite a bit.
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯在很大程度上借鉴了他的著作。

sentences.en: He argued that this was when politicians stopped being represented representatives of people.
sentences.zh: 他认为，正是在这个时候，政治家们不再是人民的代表。

sentences.en: And they just became managers of a system.
sentences.zh: 他们仅仅成为了一个系统的管理者。

sentences.en: The system became more important than the people.
sentences.zh: 系统变得比人民更重要。

sentences.en: And here's what he meant.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的意思。

sentences.zh: 当货币自由浮动，当金融市场变得过于复杂而无法控制，当全球经济开始按照其自身的内在逻辑运转时，

sentences.zh: 民选官员放弃了试图塑造它的努力，因为他们再也做不到了。

sentences.en: The system had become autonomous.
sentences.zh: 这个系统已经变得自主化。

sentences.en: Unquestionable.
sentences.zh: 不容置疑。

sentences.en: It was an implicit assumption.
sentences.zh: 这是一个隐含的假设。

sentences.en: The only choices were the way it looked, not the way that it worked.
sentences.zh: 唯一的选择是它看起来的样子，而不是它运作的方式。

sentences.en: They were aesthetic choices.
sentences.zh: 这些都是审美选择。

sentences.en: But the system already controlled all of material reality.
sentences.zh: 但这个系统已经控制了所有的物质现实。

sentences.en: So instead of representing the people to power, you know, going to powerful people and demanding change on behalf of their constituents, politicians just started in the 80s
sentences.zh: 因此，政治家们不再代表人民向权力发声——你知道的，去寻找权势人物并代表选民要求变革，而是从80年代开始，

sentences.en: representing power to the people.
sentences.zh: 转为向人民代表权力。

sentences.en: They were the spokesperson of the brand that was the power broker.
sentences.zh: 他们成了权力操纵者这个品牌的发言人。

sentences.en: And their job became explaining to citizens why nothing could ever be different.
sentences.zh: 他们的工作变成了向公民解释为什么一切都永远不可能改变。

sentences.en: Managing expectations.
sentences.zh: 管理期望。

sentences.en: Lowering ambitions.
sentences.zh: 降低雄心。

sentences.en: Curtis calls this retreat into a fake world managed by technocrats.
sentences.zh: 柯蒂斯称这种退缩为退入由技术官僚管理的虚假世界。

sentences.en: And faced with systems too complex to govern, elites built simplified models and governed those instead.
sentences.zh: 面对过于复杂而无法治理的系统，精英们构建了简化的模型，转而治理这些模型。

sentences.en: And they manipulated the representation while the territory went unattended.
sentences.zh: 他们操纵着表象，而现实的领地却无人理会。

sentences.en: And the sort of liberal gift, you know, built into this is that they would tell you that this was mature.
sentences.zh: 而这种自由主义的馈赠，你知道的，其中内置的逻辑是他们会告诉你这叫成熟。

sentences.en: When you accept that no change is ever possible, a better world's not coming, you're really just giving up the naivety of youth and realizing that
sentences.zh: 当你接受任何改变都不可能发生、一个更好的世界不会到来时，你其实只是放弃了年轻人的天真，意识到

sentences.en: you're a wise, enlightened individual who just knows that things can never change.
sentences.zh: 自己是一个精明、开明的个体，只是深知有些事情永远无法改变。

sentences.en: And the people who think that there might have been another world at another time or maybe that they could change, they're really just immature and unreasonable.
sentences.zh: 而那些认为在另一个时间可能存在另一个世界、或者认为事情可以改变的人，则纯粹是不成熟和不理智的。

sentences.zh: 他是普京在俄罗斯宣传和认知管理方面的顾问。

sentences.en: And he came from theater, actually, not politics.
sentences.zh: 实际上，他出身于戏剧界，而不是政界。

sentences.en: He understood that reality is performed and that narrative is everything.
sentences.zh: 他明白现实是表演出来的，叙事就是一切。

sentences.en: And in the early 2000s,
sentences.zh: 在2000年代初，

sentences.zh: 苏尔科夫发展了后来被称为非线性战争的理论。

sentences.en: It's called that now.
sentences.zh: 现在人们这样称呼它。

sentences.en: The traditional approach was to make propaganda.
sentences.zh: 传统的方法是制造宣传。

sentences.en: That was pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 那相当简单。

sentences.en: You just push narratives and you suppress the bad narrative.
sentences.zh: 你只需推行某种叙事，并压制不好的叙事。

sentences.en: You know, we want you to believe that Jews are bad and that they're undermining the economy.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们想让你相信犹太人是坏人，他们在破坏经济。

sentences.en: And if anyone says otherwise, we'll throw them in jail.
sentences.zh: 如果有人敢说不，我们就把他投进监狱。

sentences.en: We want you to believe that communism is good or that you need to buy war bonds.
sentences.zh: 我们想让你相信共产主义是好的，或者你需要购买战争债券。

sentences.en: And if you say something bad about it, we're going to make it very hard to people hear your voice.
sentences.zh: 如果你说了它的坏话，我们就会让你的声音很难被别人听到。

sentences.en: That's the old propaganda.
sentences.zh: 那是老一套的宣传。

sentences.en: So Surkov funded opposing groups simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 于是苏尔科夫同时资助相互对立的团体。

sentences.en: He amplified all the propaganda for all the groups.
sentences.zh: 他为所有团体的所有宣传都进行放大。

sentences.en: He suppressed nothing.
sentences.zh: 他什么都不压制。

sentences.en: In fact, he paid for it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他为此出资。

sentences.en: Nationalists, liberals,
sentences.zh: 民族主义者、自由派、

sentences.en: neo-fascists, human rights activists, feminist groups, groups on the left, groups on the right, all of them got Kremlin money to be louder and louder and louder.
sentences.zh: 新法西斯主义者、人权活动家、女权主义团体、左翼团体、右翼团体，所有这些人都拿到了克里姆林宫的资金，把声音放大、放大、再放大。

sentences.en: And then he let it be known that he was doing it.
sentences.zh: 然后他让人知道他在这么做。

sentences.en: He didn't hide it.
sentences.zh: 他并不隐瞒。

sentences.en: So it couldn't be propaganda.
sentences.zh: 所以这不可能是宣传。

sentences.en: Because the goal wasn't to make anyone believe a particular story.
sentences.zh: 因为他的目的不是让任何人相信某个特定的故事。

sentences.en: The goal was to make the truth itself unknowable.
sentences.zh: 他的目的是让真相本身变得不可知。

sentences.en: And if you can't tell who's real and who's a puppet, if every moment might be controlled opposition, if everything that you see is an act of the government and a grander narrative,
sentences.zh: 如果你分不清谁是真实的、谁是傀儡，如果每一个时刻都可能是受控的反对派，如果你看到的一切都是政府和宏大叙事的一场表演，

sentences.en: then that is the same thing that Rushkoff is talking about.
sentences.zh: 那么这与拉什科夫所谈论的是同一回事。

sentences.en: That is this broken world where everything is a data point and a story, but there can't be a story because everything is data.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个破碎的世界：一切都是数据点和故事，但又不可能存在故事，因为一切都是数据。

sentences.en: And there's no sense of time.
sentences.zh: 而且失去了时间感。

sentences.en: The information environment is so polluted that no one can verify any fact.
sentences.zh: 信息环境污染如此严重，以至于没有人能够核实任何事实。

sentences.en: And also, no one's stopping you from trying to.
sentences.zh: 同时，也没有人阻止你去尝试。

sentences.zh: 政治组织需要这种共同的现实。
